v.q: What are the three pillars of observability?
v.w: Metrics show that something is wrong, traces show where, and logs show why. Correlate them with trace ids.

v.q: Which of these is NOT a pillar of observability?
v.w: The pillars describe runtime signals. Tests are a development practice.

o: A vendor-neutral metrics facade with many registries
A new logging framework that replaces SLF4J and Logback
A message broker that carries events between services
A database driver that stores metrics inside a relational table
v.w: Spring Boot Actuator auto-configures it. You record metrics once and export them to your chosen backend.

v.q: Which statement about Micrometer is NOT true?
o: It has registries for Prometheus and others
v.w: Micrometer is for metrics. SLF4J is the logging facade.

v.q: Which is a high-cardinality tag you should avoid on a metric?
v.w: Each distinct tag combination creates a new time series. Unbounded values can overwhelm the metrics backend.

v.q: Which tag is safe on a metric?
v.w: Few distinct values keep the number of time series small. IDs create one per value.

v.q: What is the difference between a liveness and a readiness probe?
o: Liveness restarts a stuck app; readiness pauses its traffic until ready
Liveness checks the database and readiness checks the CPU
Readiness restarts the pod and liveness routes traffic
Both are the very same endpoint
v.w: Do not put slow dependency checks in liveness, or a database outage will restart every healthy pod.

v.q: Which probe failure removes the pod from traffic without a restart?
v.w: Readiness only gates traffic. Liveness restarts the container.

v.q: How do you follow one request through five services?
o: Propagate a trace id and view the spans in a tracing tool
Search the logs of each service by timestamp alone
Restart each service one after another in order
Add an extra database query to every one of the services
v.w: Micrometer Tracing and OpenTelemetry propagate the W3C `traceparent` header and create spans automatically for HTTP and messaging.

v.q: Which tool shows where one slow request spent its time across services?
v.w: Spans with durations show which hop was slow.

v.q: What is the MDC used for in logging?
o: It adds context like a trace id to each log line
It rotates the log files whenever they grow too large
It encrypts the log output before it is written to disk
It chooses the active log level for each class at run time
v.w: Spring Boot with tracing puts `traceId` and `spanId` in the MDC so every log line can be tied to a trace.

v.q: Which header carries trace context between services?
v.w: W3C Trace Context defines traceparent, and tracers add the ids to the MDC.

v.q: Which four signals does Google's SRE guidance call the golden signals?
v.w: They give a compact health view of any service. Alert on symptoms that users feel rather than on every cause.

v.q: Which pair is part of the golden signals?
v.w: The golden signals are latency, traffic, errors and saturation.

o: A reliability target, e.g. 99.9% of requests under 500 ms
A log retention policy for every node of the cluster
A special kind of load balancer placed in front of services
A contract clause that lists fixed financial penalties only
v.w: The gap between 100% and the SLO is the error budget, which guides how much risk the team can take with releases.

v.q: Which statement about SLOs is NOT true?
o: They are legal contracts with fixed penalties
They are based on measured SLIs
v.w: An SLA is the contract. An SLO is an internal target.
